cards.title: Conversations → persisted facts → patient reports
items: Gemini Live → Mobile Tool Bridge: configured input/output transcription events are text events, separate from function calls and audio.
With active transcript opt-in: Bridge → authenticated FastAPI → Conversation Service → PostgreSQL. Validate patient/session, speaker, event IDs, sequence and consent before retaining text.
Conversation Service owns opt-in history and source-linked session summaries. Without transcript opt-in, do not upload or persist conversation text; summaries use confirmed structured records only.
Observation Extraction proposes structured patient-reported facts from consented patient utterances or explicit structured answers; assistant speech and speculative emotion are not patient facts.
Patient confirms or corrects observations before they enter factual reports. Preserve source record IDs, revisions, observation time, session provenance and supersession links.
Persist confirmed observations, completed activities, feedback and assessments in the same PostgreSQL database.
Report Service reads these records, calculates deterministic factual trends and returns versioned structured JSON with source references, coverage and freshness.
FastAPI returns the same report representation to the owning Patient App and to the Doctor Portal only with a verified role, active link and sharing consent.
Raw audio/video are not stored by default. Transcripts are opt-in. No PDF generation or report file export.

Clinician request path: Doctor Portal → FastAPI → Care Link & Consent Check → Report Service → PostgreSQL. The reverse data path returns structured JSON through FastAPI only after current patient authorization is verified. The same check permits patient ownership without requiring clinician-sharing consent; clinician access requires the active patient link and sharing grant.

cards.title: Scope and ownership
items: RE:SONANCE supports patient wellbeing and follow-up after TMS treatment. Proposed architecture before implementation.
Gemini handles natural conversation; FastAPI handles trusted decisions and data; React Native renders interactive experiences; Next.js provides authorized monitoring.
The patient runtime frame nests the Gemini Function Calling / UI Bridge on device; it is not a server.
The FastAPI Backend container holds API Layer, Application Services and optional Background Jobs: logical modules in one Python application, not separate servers or microservices.
All report reads pass through FastAPI. Authentication plus ownership permits patient reads; clinician reads additionally require active link and consent.
Gemini Session Bootstrap is inside the API Layer. It obtains short-lived Gemini Live credentials through the provider API; it is not a separately deployed service.

One Application Services container includes Patient Context & Activities, Conversation Service, Observation Extraction, Care Link & Consent Check, and Report Service. These are internal Python modules of the same FastAPI backend.

cards.title: Inside the unified FastAPI Backend
items: API Layer: authentication, authorization, API routes and Gemini session bootstrap. All client HTTPS requests enter here.
Application Services: Conversation Controller, Patient Memory, Activity Recommendations, Observations, Reports, Consent and Alerts.

Application Services additionally contains Conversation Service (History + Session Summaries), Observation Extraction (Structured Patient-Reported Facts), and Report Service (record aggregation, factual trends, structured JSON). These are internal Python modules, not microservices.
Conversation Controller owns guided questions, known/missing information, policies and session state. Memory holds recovery plans, preferences and confirmed history.
Activity Recommendations covers catalog eligibility and ranking; activity sessions, configurations and feedback remain application-service responsibilities.
Observations validate explicitly patient-reported information. Reports aggregate assessments, observations, activities and trends. Alerts use predefined follow-up rules, not relapse predictions.
Consent includes care-link checks, sharing scopes and revocation. Patients read their own reports; doctors require an active link and sharing consent.
Background Jobs (optional): asynchronous report processing and notifications, with safe claiming, retries and idempotency.
These are logical modules of the same Python application. Internal arrows show calls and data flow, not network hops or separate servers.

cards.title: API routes and session bootstrap
items: Authentication and authorization validate JWTs, roles, ownership and consent before dispatch.
API routes serve activities, observations, reports, sharing controls and alerts.
Gemini session bootstrap creates an application session and obtains a restricted ephemeral credential from Gemini; the permanent key stays inside the backend.

cards.title: Session bootstrap and tool contract
items: 1–3: Patient speaks; Gemini calls present_activity_recommendations; the on-device bridge requests recommendations from FastAPI through authenticated HTTPS.
4–5: Recommendation Engine retrieves eligible activities and ranks them. FastAPI returns recommendation_id and structured data with stable backend-generated activity IDs.
6–8: Bridge renders activity cards, sends the SAME recommendations as the Gemini function response, then Gemini introduces the displayed activities verbally.
9–11: Touch or voice selects an activity from that recommendation_id; FastAPI validates and records the activity session; the app runs the experience and animation locally while Gemini can guide.
Stale or replaced recommendation batches cannot start an unoffered activity. Spoken choices and visible cards always resolve to the same backend activity IDs.
Privileged tools validate ownership, schema, session state and idempotency. Local UI animations do not need backend calls.

cards.title: Consent and confirmation gates
items: Doctor Portal → FastAPI → Care Link & Consent Check → Report Service → PostgreSQL. Check the verified doctor role, active patient relationship, patient-granted scope and expiry before querying that patient’s report records; revocation denies access.
Clinician access requires verified role, active care relationship and active sharing scope on every read.
Revocation blocks future access and pending delivery; previously viewed data cannot be retracted.
Proposed observations require patient confirmation before entering confirmed records and reports.
Sharing changes use authenticated patient controls; model claims cannot grant consent.
Background Jobs check current consent before recipient delivery; portal reads recheck access.
Patient App → FastAPI → Report Service: authenticated patients can view their own reports without clinician-sharing consent.
Doctor Portal → FastAPI → Consent Check → Report Service: verified clinicians need an active patient relationship and active report scope.
The access-check module branches by caller: patient ownership or clinician link plus consent. It is not a requirement that patients consent to read their own reports.

cards.title: Durable processing and reports
items: An accepted write and its outbox event commit in the same database transaction.
Optional Background Jobs claim durable jobs and reuse backend domain rules; execution may repeat and handlers deduplicate.
Reports expose time range, missing data, sources, version and last refresh time.
Alerts move from open to acknowledged to resolved; delivery and acknowledgement are separate.
Portal polls authorized endpoints initially. Reports remain in-app; no PDF generation or export.
Application Services → PostgreSQL Outbox → optional Background Jobs → PostgreSQL. Jobs handle async report processing and notifications; synchronous API/tool actions do not wait for them.

cards.title: Media, avatar and recovery
items: Audio and optional camera frames stream directly between the app and Gemini.
Rive renders locally using idle, listening, thinking, speaking and interrupted playback states.
Gemini resumption state is separate from persisted application progress.
Reconnects retain accepted records; tool retries cannot duplicate observations or completions.
Validate native capture, playback, interruption, camera and Rive on physical devices.
Bridge synchronizes touch and voice selection, updates React Native state, and triggers local activity animation. Rive is rendered on-device, never streamed AI video.

The mobile bridge owns Tool Calls, Activity Cards, Voice/Touch Selection and UI State. It requests backend recommendations, renders interactive cards, then returns the same IDs to Gemini for verbal presentation.

cards.title: Data and operational boundaries
items: Supabase Auth issues identity tokens; the separate Tiger Data database stores application records.
Clients never connect directly to application PostgreSQL; FastAPI enforces authorization.

Raw audio/video are not stored by default. Conversation transcript persistence is opt-in and checked by FastAPI on every ingestion; structured memory and confirmed records have separate retention rules.
Redact health content and credentials from logs; audit clinician access and sensitive changes.
Minimize Gemini context; decide provider retention, regions, deletion and backup expiry before real patient data.

Single application source of truth: users/profiles; care links/consent; conversation sessions; memory/observations; recovery plans; catalog/sessions/feedback; assessments; reports/metadata; alerts/audit/outbox.

cards.title: Deployment and unresolved decisions
items: Mobile app, Next.js portal and one unified FastAPI Backend are the application boundaries. Background Jobs are an optional module inside that backend.
Modal or Vultr remains a hosting decision. No separate worker server or microservice is specified.
Codex + Entire support development and are outside the runtime request path.
Model/API version, clinician verification, rule thresholds, retention and performance targets remain open.
Direct patient help controls do not depend on a Gemini tool call. No diagnosis or promise of emergency monitoring.

cards.title: Identity and Gemini credentials are separate
items: Patient App / Doctor Portal → Supabase Auth: login. Supabase Auth → client: JWT. Client → FastAPI: authenticated HTTPS; FastAPI verifies JWT using trusted keys.

Patient App → FastAPI: live-session request. FastAPI API Layer → internal Gemini Session Bootstrap: obtain a restricted short-lived Gemini Live credential through the provider API. FastAPI → Patient App: ephemeral token.
Patient App ↔ Gemini Live: direct secure WebSocket. Supabase Auth does not generate Gemini tokens.
Gemini Session Bootstrap is backend logic, not another server. The provider API issues the credential; permanent API keys stay on the backend.
